column3: The Hebrew has tongue, sword, arrow, and bitter word in the singular; BSB uses plural tongues, swords, words, and arrows.
The Hebrew repeats the root of searching and calls the inward part and heart deep; BSB describes a secret plan and calls them mysterious.
The Hebrew narrates God shooting and wounds occurring as completed actions, and names one arrow; BSB uses future verbs and plural arrows.
The Hebrew uses an active causing him to stumble and a singular tongue; BSB uses passive stumbling and plural tongues. Head-shaking is not explicitly named in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew narrates fearing, declaring, and understanding with completed forms; BSB gives future actions.
